inventory.producer: The ordered act-step list of `### Step 4: Update Way-of-Working` in setup-pm SKILL.md — grammar `<ordinal>. **<title>**: <body>` at column 0. Its LITERAL ordinals are the only thing a `step N` back-reference written inside that list can resolve against (a skill is fed to the agent as markdown source, never as rendered HTML).
inputs: the Step 4 act-step list as it stands at 643d24f5 (7 steps: Check, fields, `## State Mapping`, report-unresolved, `## Git Workflow`, `## Assignment`, Verify)
the `## Assignment` act-step condition "When step 3 just declared a separate `code-host`"
representations: .claude/skills/pair-capability-setup-pm/SKILL.md:107 — generated mirror, produced by the `pair update` name transform; byte-identical for this sentence
consumers: the agent executing /pair-capability-setup-pm for a hosts-no-code tool (linear, jira, filesystem): it evaluates the condition to decide whether to ask for, and write, `code-host-assignee`
way-of-working.md `## Assignment` → `code-host-assignee` (the downstream adoption key; unwritten ⇒ PRs on the separate code host are filed under the wrong identifier or unassigned)
classes: C-correct: the back-reference cites the ordinal the `## Git Workflow` act-step actually carries
C-stale: it cites an EXISTING but different act-step — the condition is evaluable and silently false forever (the defect at 643d24f5: cites 3, which is `## State Mapping` and declares no code-host)
C-outofrange: it cites an ordinal the list does not contain
C-missing-referent: the `## Git Workflow` act-step is deleted or retitled, leaving nothing to resolve against
C-missing-citation: the back-reference sentence is deleted rather than corrected — the condition disappears instead of firing
C-semantic: the act-step at the cited ordinal is not the one that declares `code-host` (the referent by meaning, independent of position)
C-hosts-code: the selected PM tool hosts its own code (GitHub Projects, Azure DevOps), so no `code-host` is declared and the condition is correctly false
interactions: ordinal derivation × corpus mirror: the canonical source is corrected and the generated mirror is not re-synced with the real `pair update` transform, so the copy that actually ships keeps the defect
renumbering × back-reference: inserting or removing an act-step changes the ordinal a correct back-reference must carry — the exact mechanism that produced this defect

matrix.oracle: n/a — no executable oracle at this producer
matrix.rationale: The producer is ONE sentence of skill text; it does not branch per tool. The hosts-code/hosts-no-code split lives in act-step 5 and in way-of-working-pm-resolution.md, and the only obligation observable at this producer is that the back-reference resolves to the act-step that declares `code-host` — already covered by W3/W4. Asserting a per-tool outcome here would require executing the skill against a live tool, which no assertion in this corpus does.
